findings.text: resolve_launch_executable gained a `backend` parameter that no production caller passes — reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3164 and reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1332 and :1849 all call it with only `facts` — so the composed-plan resolution still reads the host layer by name at :1229 and a project-layer-only declaration that preflight accepts at :1172 is refused when the plan is built; the evidence fragment's claim at docs/evidence/fragments/a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker/a-launch-finds-its-backend-on-the-declared-path.html:27 that "the plan resolution ... pass[es] their project-resolved entry through" is contradicted by those call sites, and no test covers the composition path with a project layer

_persisted_worker_environment composes the worker PATH through launch_search_path with the backend name alone, so a project-layer search_path never reaches the worker's own PATH; the composed environment carries the directory only for a host-layer declaration, which is the case the plan measured and tests/test_a_launch_finds_its_backend_on_the_declared_path.py:88 exercises

the manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite `command` values end in "<52 importer test files under the base extraction>" and "<53 importer test files in the worktree, resolved over its own tree>", which are descriptions rather than the literal commands the contract requires, so neither arm can be re-run as recorded
